chapter: Paris scene and a visit home, 1937-39
title: The Kentucky Singers' spirituals in Paris
summary: Mabel Mercer's sound and the four unaccompanied Kentucky Singers who could set a room on fire with spirituals.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: You see, Mabel Mercer, I keep talking about her, because she had that most beautiful sound singing and you had the Kentucky singers and you had a man calles Strut Payne.
What did the Kentucky singers do?
Kentucky singers, they sang spirituals and Negro songs. They called them Negro songs and everything and they would set you on fire.
How many of them were there?
Four of them. They would set you on fire. Don't care where they went, they -- when they got finished, it could be raining out there.
Did they use instruments or do it a capello?
